beats.text: Every time your GPU runs an LLM, it spends 90% of its time waiting for data to travel from slow VRAM to the fast compute cores.
beats.visual_focus: A glowing H100 chip struggling to pull data from a massive, distant VRAM reservoir.

beats.text: Think of it like a bucket brigade: if the runners are faster than the water source, they just stand there. That's your GPU idle cycle.
beats.visual_focus: Animated stick figures passing buckets; the source is a trickle, the runners are blurred with speed.

beats.text: FlashAttention-3 solves this with kernel fusion. It keeps data in the chip's tiny, ultra-fast SRAM, performing massive matrix operations without ever hitting main memory.
beats.visual_focus: A zoomed-in view of the H100 SM (Streaming Multiprocessor) locking data inside a glowing SRAM cache box.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: The hook was solid—I'm definitely tired of seeing my GPU utilization tank because of memory bottlenecks. I liked the bucket brigade analogy, it wasn't too 'baby-talk' and actually made sense. However, in Beat 4, you threw 'overlapping asynchronous I/O' at me. I get the gist, but it's a bit of a buzzword-heavy way to describe just doing two things at once. You almost lost me there, but the TFLOPS number brought me back.
